from typing import List


class Solution:
    def longestSpecialPath(self, edges: List[List[int]], nums: List[int]) -> List[int]:
        n = len(nums)
        m = len(edges)

        # adjacency in flat arrays (fast, no recursion)
        head = [-1] * n
        nxt = [0] * (2 * m)
        to = [0] * (2 * m)
        wt = [0] * (2 * m)
        idx = 0
        for u, v, w in edges:
            to[idx] = v; wt[idx] = w; nxt[idx] = head[u]; head[u] = idx; idx += 1
            to[idx] = u; wt[idx] = w; nxt[idx] = head[v]; head[v] = idx; idx += 1

        maxval = max(nums) if n else 0
        last = [[] for _ in range(maxval + 1)]   # value -> stack of depths on current root path
        prefix = [0] * (n + 1)                   # prefix[d] = distance root -> node at depth d

        best_len = 0
        best_nodes = 1

        # stack items: (0, node, parent, left, depth, dist) = enter ; (1, value) = exit
        stack = [(0, 0, -1, 0, 0, 0)]
        while stack:
            item = stack.pop()
            if item[0] == 1:
                last[item[1]].pop()
                continue

            _, u, p, left, depth, dist = item
            prefix[depth] = dist

            val = nums[u]
            lst = last[val]
            if lst:
                cand = lst[-1] + 1
                if cand > left:
                    left = cand
            lst.append(depth)
            stack.append((1, val))

            cur_len = dist - prefix[left]
            cur_nodes = depth - left + 1
            if cur_len > best_len or (cur_len == best_len and cur_nodes < best_nodes):
                best_len = cur_len
                best_nodes = cur_nodes

            e = head[u]
            while e != -1:
                w = to[e]
                if w != p:
                    stack.append((0, w, u, left, depth + 1, dist + wt[e]))
                e = nxt[e]

        return [best_len, best_nodes]

from typing import List
from collections import defaultdict


class Solution:
    def longestSpecialPath(self, edges: List[List[int]], nums: List[int]) -> List[int]:
        n = len(nums)
        if n == 0:
            return [0, 0]

        g = [[] for _ in range(n)]
        for u, v, w in edges:
            g[u].append((v, w))
            g[v].append((u, w))

        # dis[d] = distancia desde la raiz al nodo de profundidad d en el camino actual
        dis = [0]
        # last[valor] = pila de profundidades donde aparece ese valor en el camino actual
        last = defaultdict(list)

        best_len = 0
        best_nodes = 1

        # Se entra a la raiz
        last[nums[0]].append(0)

        # frame: (nodo, padre, profundidad, top, iterador de vecinos)
        # top = menor indice de profundidad admisible como inicio del camino especial
        stack = [(0, -1, 0, 0, iter(g[0]))]

        while stack:
            node, parent, depth, top, it = stack[-1]
            advanced = False
            for child, w in it:
                if child == parent:
                    continue
                cd = depth + 1
                nd = dis[depth] + w
                if len(dis) <= cd:
                    dis.append(nd)
                else:
                    dis[cd] = nd

                cval = nums[child]
                lst = last[cval]
                ntop = top
                if lst and lst[-1] + 1 > ntop:
                    ntop = lst[-1] + 1
                lst.append(cd)

                length = dis[cd] - dis[ntop]
                cnt = cd - ntop + 1
                if length > best_len or (length == best_len and cnt < best_nodes):
                    best_len = length
                    best_nodes = cnt

                stack.append((child, node, cd, ntop, iter(g[child])))
                advanced = True
                break

            if not advanced:
                last[nums[node]].pop()
                stack.pop()

        return [best_len, best_nodes]

from typing import List


class Solution:
    def maxSubarraySum(self, nums: List[int]) -> int:
        n = len(nums)
        mx = max(nums)

        # If every element is negative, the best subarray is a single element and
        # removing occurrences of any value can only take options away.
        if mx < 0:
            return mx

        # Kadane on the untouched array (>= 0 since mx >= 0).
        ans = 0
        cur = 0
        for v in nums:
            cur += v
            if cur < 0:
                cur = 0
            elif cur > ans:
                ans = cur

        # Only removing a NEGATIVE value can help: for an interval [l, r] the sum
        # after removing x is sum(l..r) - x * count_x(l..r) <= sum(l..r) when x >= 0.
        groups = {}
        for i, v in enumerate(nums):
            if v < 0:
                g = groups.get(v)
                if g is None:
                    groups[v] = [i]
                else:
                    g.append(i)
        if not groups:
            return ans

        # Max-subarray segment tree: (tot, pre, suf, best) per node.
        size = 1
        while size < n or size < 2:
            size <<= 1
        NEG = -(1 << 40)  # far below any real sum (|sum| <= 1e5 * 1e6 = 1e11 < 2**40)
        tot = [0] * (2 * size)
        pre = [NEG] * (2 * size)
        suf = [NEG] * (2 * size)
        bst = [NEG] * (2 * size)

        for i in range(n):
            v = nums[i]
            j = size + i
            tot[j] = v
            pre[j] = v
            suf[j] = v
            bst[j] = v

        for j in range(size - 1, 0, -1):
            l = j << 1
            r = l | 1
            tl = tot[l]
            tr = tot[r]
            tot[j] = tl + tr
            a = pre[l]
            b = tl + pre[r]
            pre[j] = a if a > b else b
            a = suf[r]
            b = tr + suf[l]
            suf[j] = a if a > b else b
            a = bst[l]
            b = bst[r]
            if b > a:
                a = b
            b = suf[l] + pre[r]
            bst[j] = a if a > b else b

        def update(idxs, val):
            """Set every position in idxs to val and repair the tree."""
            if len(idxs) == 1:
                j = size + idxs[0]
                tot[j] = val
                pre[j] = val
                suf[j] = val
                bst[j] = val
                j >>= 1
                while j:
                    l = j << 1
                    r = l | 1
                    tl = tot[l]
                    tr = tot[r]
                    tot[j] = tl + tr
                    a = pre[l]
                    b = tl + pre[r]
                    pre[j] = a if a > b else b
                    a = suf[r]
                    b = tr + suf[l]
                    suf[j] = a if a > b else b
                    a = bst[l]
                    b = bst[r]
                    if b > a:
                        a = b
                    b = suf[l] + pre[r]
                    bst[j] = a if a > b else b
                    j >>= 1
                return

            nodes = set()
            for i in idxs:
                j = size + i
                tot[j] = val
                pre[j] = val
                suf[j] = val
                bst[j] = val
                nodes.add(j >> 1)
            # Level-synchronous rebuild: all touched leaves share the same depth.
            while nodes:
                for j in nodes:
                    l = j << 1
                    r = l | 1
                    tl = tot[l]
                    tr = tot[r]
                    tot[j] = tl + tr
                    a = pre[l]
                    b = tl + pre[r]
                    pre[j] = a if a > b else b
                    a = suf[r]
                    b = tr + suf[l]
                    suf[j] = a if a > b else b
                    a = bst[l]
                    b = bst[r]
                    if b > a:
                        a = b
                    b = suf[l] + pre[r]
                    bst[j] = a if a > b else b
                nodes = {j >> 1 for j in nodes if j > 1}

        for v, idxs in groups.items():
            update(idxs, 0)      # "remove" every occurrence of v
            best = bst[1]
            if best > ans:
                ans = best
            update(idxs, v)      # restore

        return ans

from typing import List


class Solution:
    def maxSubarraySum(self, nums: List[int]) -> int:
        n = len(nums)
        NEG = -(1 << 60)

        # 1) Best subarray of the original array (Kadane, non-empty).
        best_ans = NEG
        cur = 0
        for v in nums:
            cur = v if cur < 0 else cur + v
            if cur > best_ans:
                best_ans = cur

        # If the best is <= 0 then every element is <= 0, and removing any value
        # can only shrink the pool of candidates -> answer is already optimal.
        if best_ans <= 0:
            return best_ans

        # Only removing a NEGATIVE value can ever help: for x >= 0 any subarray of
        # the reduced array has sum = sum(range) - x*count <= sum(range).
        pos = {}
        for i, v in enumerate(nums):
            if v < 0:
                lst = pos.get(v)
                if lst is None:
                    pos[v] = [i]
                else:
                    lst.append(i)
        if not pos:
            return best_ans

        # 2) Segment tree over (total, best prefix, best suffix, best subarray).
        size = 1
        while size < n:
            size <<= 1
        tot = [0] * (2 * size)
        pre = [NEG] * (2 * size)
        suf = [NEG] * (2 * size)
        bst = [NEG] * (2 * size)

        for i, v in enumerate(nums):
            j = size + i
            tot[j] = v
            pre[j] = v
            suf[j] = v
            bst[j] = v

        for j in range(size - 1, 0, -1):
            l = j << 1
            r = l | 1
            tl = tot[l]
            tr = tot[r]
            sl = suf[l]
            pr = pre[r]
            tot[j] = tl + tr
            a = tl + pr
            b = pre[l]
            pre[j] = b if b > a else a
            a = tr + sl
            b = suf[r]
            suf[j] = b if b > a else a
            a = sl + pr
            b = bst[l]
            c = bst[r]
            if c > b:
                b = c
            bst[j] = b if b > a else a

        def update(i, val, tot=tot, pre=pre, suf=suf, bst=bst, size=size):
            j = size + i
            tot[j] = val
            pre[j] = val
            suf[j] = val
            bst[j] = val
            j >>= 1
            while j:
                l = j << 1
                r = l | 1
                tl = tot[l]
                tr = tot[r]
                sl = suf[l]
                pr = pre[r]
                tot[j] = tl + tr
                a = tl + pr
                b = pre[l]
                pre[j] = b if b > a else a
                a = tr + sl
                b = suf[r]
                suf[j] = b if b > a else a
                a = sl + pr
                b = bst[l]
                c = bst[r]
                if c > b:
                    b = c
                bst[j] = b if b > a else a
                j >>= 1

        # 3) For each distinct negative value, zero out its positions (removing it
        # from the array is equivalent to turning it into a neutral 0 for sums),
        # query the global best subarray, then restore.
        # An all-zero window could report a spurious 0, but best_ans > 0 here, so
        # such a candidate can never win.
        for x, ps in pos.items():
            if len(ps) == n:
                continue  # array would become empty: not allowed
            for i in ps:
                update(i, 0)
            v = bst[1]
            if v > best_ans:
                best_ans = v
            for i in ps:
                update(i, x)

        return best_ans

import sys
import numpy as np


def main():
    data = sys.stdin.buffer.read().split()
    n = int(data[0]); P = int(data[1])
    MAXE = n * (n - 1) // 2

    # Pascal triangle
    Cb = [[0] * (n + 1) for _ in range(n + 1)]
    for i in range(n + 1):
        Cb[i][0] = 1
        for j in range(1, i + 1):
            Cb[i][j] = Cb[i - 1][j - 1] + Cb[i - 1][j]
    # (1+x)^k mod P
    pw = [[Cb[k][j] % P for j in range(k + 1)] for k in range(n + 1)]

    # mult[a][b] = ((1+x)^a - 1) * (1+x)^b   (edges of a new vertex: >=1 to prev layer,
    # any subset to the b vertices already placed in the current layer)
    mult = [[None] * (n + 1) for _ in range(n + 1)]
    for a in range(1, n + 1):
        qa = pw[a][:]
        qa[0] = 0
        for b in range(n + 1):
            pb = pw[b]
            res = [0] * (a + b + 1)
            for i in range(1, a + 1):
                ci = qa[i]
                if ci:
                    for j in range(b + 1):
                        res[i + j] = (res[i + j] + ci * pb[j]) % P
            mult[a][b] = res

    facts = [1] * (n + 1)
    f = 1
    for i in range(1, n + 1):
        f = f * i % P
        facts[i] = f
    invf = [pow(facts[i], P - 2, P) for i in range(n + 1)]

    # state: (a = size of previous complete layer, b = size of current partial layer)
    # rows indexed by j with F = 2*j - t, t = T - b ; polynomial in x = number of edges
    cur = {}
    a0 = np.zeros((2, 1), dtype=np.int64)
    a0[1, 0] = 1          # T=1, a=1, b=0, t=1, F=1  -> j=1
    cur[(1, 0)] = a0

    ans = np.zeros(MAXE + 1, dtype=np.int64)
    T = 1
    while True:
        cap = T * (T - 1) // 2 + 1
        # close layers: (a,b) -> (b,0), F -> b-F , times 1/b!
        closed = {}
        for (a, b), src in cur.items():
            if b == 0:
                continue
            t = T - b
            invb = invf[b]
            Ls = min(src.shape[1], cap)
            tgt = closed.get(b)
            if tgt is None:
                tgt = np.zeros((T + 1, cap), dtype=np.int64)
                closed[b] = tgt
            tgt[b:b + t + 1, :Ls] += (src[::-1, :Ls] * invb) % P
        for b, tgt in closed.items():
            tgt %= P
            cur[(b, 0)] = tgt

        if T == n:
            half = n // 2      # F = 0
            for (a, b), arrx in cur.items():
                if b == 0:
                    w = arrx.shape[1]
                    ans[:w] += arrx[half]
            ans %= P
            break

        # add one vertex to the current layer
        scal = n - T
        newcap = (T + 1) * T // 2 + 1
        nxt = {}
        for (a, b), src in cur.items():
            m = mult[a][b]
            Ls = src.shape[1]
            R = src.shape[0]
            L = min(Ls + a + b, newcap)
            dst = np.zeros((R, L), dtype=np.int64)
            cnt = 0
            for k in range(1, a + b + 1):
                if k >= L:
                    break
                cc = m[k] * scal % P
                if cc == 0:
                    continue
                e = min(k + Ls, L)
                dst[:, k:e] += cc * src[:, :e - k]
                cnt += 1
                if cnt >= 8:
                    dst %= P
                    cnt = 0
            if cnt:
                dst %= P
            nxt[(a, b + 1)] = dst
        cur = nxt
        T += 1

    out = ' '.join(str(int(ans[M])) for M in range(n - 1, MAXE + 1))
    sys.stdout.write(out + '\n')

import sys
from math import comb

import numpy as np


def main():
    data = sys.stdin.buffer.read().split()
    N = int(data[0])
    P = int(data[1])

    H = N // 2
    D = N * (N - 1) // 2

    # factorials / inverse factorials mod P (P is prime >= 1e8 > N, so all invertible)
    fact = [1] * (N + 2)
    for i in range(1, N + 2):
        fact[i] = fact[i - 1] * i % P
    invfact = [1] * (N + 2)
    invfact[N + 1] = pow(fact[N + 1], P - 2, P)
    for i in range(N + 1, 0, -1):
        invfact[i - 1] = invfact[i] * i % P

    # polynomial length (in y = 1+x) for a prefix using u vertices: degree <= C(u,2)
    L = [u * (u - 1) // 2 + 1 for u in range(N + 1)]

    # dp[(p, a, u)] = int64 array of shape (H+1, L[u])
    #   p = parity of the index of the last completed layer
    #   a = size of that layer
    #   u = vertices used so far
    #   rows indexed by e = number of vertices at even distance so far
    #   cols indexed by degree in y = 1+x
    dp = {}
    start = np.zeros((H + 1, L[1]), dtype=np.int64)
    start[1, 0] = 1 % P
    dp[(0, 1, 1)] = start

    for u in range(1, N):
        keys_u = [k for k in dp if k[2] == u]
        for key in keys_u:
            src = dp[key]
            if not src.any():
                continue
            p, a, _ = key
            p2 = 1 - p
            Lu = L[u]
            if p2 == 0:
                if H + 1 - 1 <= 0:
                    continue
            for b in range(1, N - u + 1):
                if p2 == 0:
                    if b > H:
                        continue
                    drow = slice(b, H + 1)
                    srow = slice(0, H + 1 - b)
                else:
                    drow = slice(0, H + 1)
                    srow = slice(0, H + 1)
                sub = src[srow]
                if sub.shape[0] == 0:
                    continue
                nu = u + b
                nkey = (p2, b, nu)
                dest = dp.get(nkey)
                if dest is None:
                    dest = np.zeros((H + 1, L[nu]), dtype=np.int64)
                    dp[nkey] = dest
                sb = b * (b - 1) // 2
                inv_b = invfact[b]
                touched = False
                # multiplier: (y^a - 1)^b * y^{C(b,2)} / b!
                for t in range(b + 1):
                    c = comb(b, t) % P * inv_b % P
                    if (b - t) & 1:
                        c = (-c) % P
                    if c == 0:
                        continue
                    s = a * t + sb
                    dest[drow, s:s + Lu] += (c * sub) % P
                    touched = True
                if touched:
                    dest %= P

    # collect final generating function in y
    cy = [0] * (D + 1)
    for key, arr in dp.items():
        if key[2] == N:
            row = arr[H]
            n = row.shape[0]
            for d in range(n):
                v = int(row[d])
                if v:
                    cy[d] = (cy[d] + v) % P

    # binomials mod P up to D
    C = [[0] * (D + 1) for _ in range(D + 1)]
    for n in range(D + 1):
        Cn = C[n]
        Cn[0] = 1 % P
        if n:
            Cp = C[n - 1]
            for k in range(1, n + 1):
                Cn[k] = (Cp[k - 1] + Cp[k]) % P

    f = fact[N - 1]
    out = []
    for M in range(N - 1, D + 1):
        s = 0
        for d in range(M, D + 1):
            cd = cy[d]
            if cd:
                s += cd * C[d][M]
        out.append(str(s % P * f % P))

    sys.stdout.write(" ".join(out) + "\n")


main()

from bisect import bisect_right
from typing import List


class Solution:
    def maximumWeight(self, intervals: List[List[int]]) -> List[int]:
        n = len(intervals)

        # Ordenamos los indices por extremo izquierdo (desempate por derecho).
        order = sorted(range(n), key=lambda i: (intervals[i][0], intervals[i][1]))
        ls = [intervals[i][0] for i in order]

        # dp[i][j] = (mejor peso, tupla de indices originales ordenada ascendentemente)
        # usando intervalos de la posicion ordenada i en adelante y eligiendo a lo sumo j.
        EMPTY = (0, ())
        dp = [[EMPTY] * 5 for _ in range(n + 1)]

        for i in range(n - 1, -1, -1):
            idx = order[i]
            l, r, w = intervals[idx]
            # Primera posicion cuyo l es estrictamente mayor que r (no comparten punto).
            nxt = bisect_right(ls, r)

            skip_row = dp[i + 1]
            take_row = dp[nxt]

            new_row = [EMPTY] * 5
            for j in range(1, 5):
                bw, bt = skip_row[j]          # opcion: no tomar el intervalo i
                sw, st = take_row[j - 1]      # opcion: tomarlo
                cw = sw + w
                if st:
                    ct = tuple(sorted(st + (idx,)))
                else:
                    ct = (idx,)
                # Maximizar peso; a igual peso, tupla lexicograficamente menor.
                if cw > bw or (cw == bw and ct < bt):
                    bw, bt = cw, ct
                new_row[j] = (bw, bt)

            dp[i] = new_row

        return list(dp[0][4][1])

from bisect import bisect_right
from typing import List


class Solution:
    def maximumWeight(self, intervals: List[List[int]]) -> List[int]:
        n = len(intervals)
        K = 4

        # Ordenar por extremo izquierdo, conservando el indice original.
        order = sorted(range(n), key=lambda i: intervals[i][0])
        L = [intervals[i][0] for i in order]
        R = [intervals[i][1] for i in order]
        W = [intervals[i][2] for i in order]
        IDX = order

        # nxt[i] = primer intervalo (en el orden) cuyo l es estrictamente mayor que r_i.
        # Compartir un extremo cuenta como solapar, por eso bisect_right sobre r_i.
        nxt = [bisect_right(L, R[i]) for i in range(n)]

        # dp[k][i] = (peso maximo, lista de indices ordenada lexicograficamente minima)
        # eligiendo a lo sumo k intervalos entre los que empiezan en la posicion i o despues.
        empty = (0, [])
        dp = [[empty] * (n + 1) for _ in range(K + 1)]

        for i in range(n - 1, -1, -1):
            j = nxt[i]
            wi = W[i]
            idi = IDX[i]
            for k in range(1, K + 1):
                bw, bl = dp[k][i + 1]          # no tomar el intervalo i
                tw, tl = dp[k - 1][j]          # tomarlo y saltar a los compatibles
                cw = tw + wi
                if cw > bw:
                    dp[k][i] = (cw, sorted(tl + [idi]))
                elif cw == bw:
                    cl = sorted(tl + [idi])
                    dp[k][i] = (cw, cl) if cl < bl else (bw, bl)
                else:
                    dp[k][i] = (bw, bl)

        return dp[K][0][1]

class Solution:
    def countWinningSequences(self, s: str) -> int:
        MOD = 10**9 + 7
        idx = {'F': 0, 'W': 1, 'E': 2}
        # beat[x] = the creature that x defeats
        # Fire (F) beats Earth (E); Water (W) beats Fire (F); Earth (E) beats Water (W)
        beat = [2, 0, 1]

        a = [idx[c] for c in s]
        n = len(a)
        size = 2 * n + 1
        off = n

        def score(b, ai):
            if beat[b] == ai:
                return 1
            if beat[ai] == b:
                return -1
            return 0

        # dp[b][d + off] = number of valid Bob prefixes ending with move b and score diff d
        dp = [[0] * size for _ in range(3)]
        a0 = a[0]
        for b in range(3):
            dp[b][off + score(b, a0)] += 1

        for i in range(1, n):
            ai = a[i]
            lo = off - i
            hi = off + i
            d0, d1, d2 = dp[0], dp[1], dp[2]
            total = [0] * size
            for d in range(lo, hi + 1):
                total[d] = (d0[d] + d1[d] + d2[d]) % MOD

            ndp = [[0] * size for _ in range(3)]
            for b in range(3):
                sc = score(b, ai)
                row = dp[b]
                nrow = ndp[b]
                for d in range(lo, hi + 1):
                    v = total[d] - row[d]
                    if v:
                        t = d + sc
                        nrow[t] = (nrow[t] + v) % MOD
            dp = ndp

        ans = 0
        for b in range(3):
            row = dp[b]
            for d in range(off + 1, size):
                ans += row[d]
        return ans % MOD

class Solution:
    def findAnswer(self, parent: List[int], s: str) -> List[bool]:
        n = len(parent)

        # Hijos en orden creciente (i crece, asi que cada lista ya queda ordenada)
        children = [[] for _ in range(n)]
        for i in range(1, n):
            children[parent[i]].append(i)

        # Recorrido post-orden iterativo: construye el dfsStr completo desde la raiz
        # y guarda, para cada nodo x, el intervalo [lo[x], hi[x]] que ocupa su subarbol.
        lo = [0] * n
        hi = [0] * n
        buf = []
        stack = [(0, 0)]
        while stack:
            x, ci = stack.pop()
            if ci == 0:
                lo[x] = len(buf)
            cs = children[x]
            if ci < len(cs):
                stack.append((x, ci + 1))
                stack.append((cs[ci], 0))
            else:
                hi[x] = len(buf)
                buf.append(s[x])

        t = "".join(buf)
        m = len(t)

        # Manacher: d1[i] = radio de palindromos impares centrados en i,
        #           d2[i] = radio de palindromos pares con centro entre i-1 e i.
        d1 = [0] * m
        l, r = 0, -1
        for i in range(m):
            k = 1 if i > r else min(d1[l + r - i], r - i + 1)
            while i - k >= 0 and i + k < m and t[i - k] == t[i + k]:
                k += 1
            d1[i] = k
            k -= 1
            if i + k > r:
                l = i - k
                r = i + k

        d2 = [0] * m
        l, r = 0, -1
        for i in range(m):
            k = 0 if i > r else min(d2[l + r - i + 1], r - i + 1)
            while i - k - 1 >= 0 and i + k < m and t[i - k - 1] == t[i + k]:
                k += 1
            d2[i] = k
            k -= 1
            if i + k > r:
                l = i - k - 1
                r = i + k

        answer = [False] * n
        for i in range(n):
            a, b = lo[i], hi[i]
            length = b - a + 1
            if length & 1:
                c = (a + b) // 2
                answer[i] = d1[c] >= (length + 1) // 2
            else:
                c = (a + b + 1) // 2
                answer[i] = d2[c] >= length // 2
        return answer

class Solution:
    def numberOfWays(self, n: int, x: int, y: int) -> int:
        MOD = 10**9 + 7
        m = min(n, x)

        # Stirling numbers of the second kind S(n, k) for k = 0..m
        # S(i, k) = k * S(i-1, k) + S(i-1, k-1)
        S = [0] * (m + 1)
        S[0] = 1
        for i in range(1, n + 1):
            # iterate k downwards to reuse the previous row in place
            top = min(i, m)
            for k in range(top, 0, -1):
                S[k] = (k * S[k] + S[k - 1]) % MOD
            S[0] = 0

        ans = 0
        perm = 1  # P(x, k) = x * (x-1) * ... * (x-k+1)
        ypow = 1  # y^k
        for k in range(1, m + 1):
            perm = perm * ((x - k + 1) % MOD) % MOD
            ypow = ypow * y % MOD
            if perm == 0:
                break
            ans = (ans + S[k] * perm % MOD * ypow) % MOD

        return ans % MOD

class Solution:
    def numberOfWays(self, n: int, x: int, y: int) -> int:
        MOD = 10**9 + 7
        m = min(n, x)

        # Stirling numbers of the second kind: S(n, k) for k = 0..m
        # dp[j] = S(i, j), built row by row.
        dp = [0] * (m + 1)
        dp[0] = 1
        for i in range(1, n + 1):
            # iterate downwards so dp[j-1] is still S(i-1, j-1)
            top = min(i, m)
            for j in range(top, 0, -1):
                dp[j] = (j * dp[j] + dp[j - 1]) % MOD
            dp[0] = 0

        ans = 0
        perm = 1        # falling factorial x*(x-1)*...*(x-k+1)
        ypow = 1        # y^k
        for k in range(1, m + 1):
            perm = perm * ((x - k + 1) % MOD) % MOD
            ypow = ypow * y % MOD
            ans = (ans + dp[k] * perm % MOD * ypow) % MOD

        return ans % MOD

class Solution:
    def subsequencePairCount(self, nums: List[int]) -> int:
        MOD = 10**9 + 7
        M = 201

        # Conjunto de valores alcanzables como GCD de algun subconjunto.
        S = set()
        for x in nums:
            S |= {gcd(x, s) for s in S}
            S.add(x)
        vals = [0] + sorted(S)   # 0 representa "subsecuencia vacia"

        # Tablas de gcd precomputadas por cada valor distinto de nums.
        gt = [None] * M
        for x in set(nums):
            gt[x] = [gcd(x, v) for v in range(M)]

        # dp[a][b] = numero de formas de repartir los elementos vistos
        # de modo que gcd(seq1)=a y gcd(seq2)=b (0 = vacia).
        dp = [[0] * M for _ in range(M)]
        dp[0][0] = 1

        for x in nums:
            gx = gt[x]
            ndp = [row[:] for row in dp]      # opcion: no usar x
            for a in vals:
                row = dp[a]
                na = gx[a]
                nrow_a = ndp[na]              # x va a seq1
                row_a = ndp[a]                # x va a seq2
                for b in vals:
                    c = row[b]
                    if c:
                        nrow_a[b] = (nrow_a[b] + c) % MOD
                        nb = gx[b]
                        row_a[nb] = (row_a[nb] + c) % MOD
            dp = ndp

        ans = 0
        for g in vals:
            if g:
                ans += dp[g][g]
        return ans % MOD

class Solution:
    def countBalancedPermutations(self, num: str) -> int:
        MOD = 10**9 + 7

        # Guardar la entrada a mitad de la funcion, como pide el enunciado.
        velunexorai = num

        n = len(velunexorai)
        digits = [int(ch) for ch in velunexorai]
        total = sum(digits)
        if total % 2 == 1:
            return 0

        target = total // 2          # suma que deben tener las posiciones pares
        E = (n + 1) // 2             # numero de indices pares (0,2,4,...)
        O = n // 2                   # numero de indices impares (1,3,5,...)

        cnt = Counter(digits)

        # dp[j][s] = numero de formas (contando permutaciones distintas) de haber
        # colocado los digitos procesados hasta ahora usando j huecos pares,
        # con suma s en los huecos pares.
        dp = [[0] * (target + 1) for _ in range(E + 1)]
        dp[0][0] = 1

        placed = 0
        for d in range(10):
            c = cnt.get(d, 0)
            if c == 0:
                continue

            ndp = [[0] * (target + 1) for _ in range(E + 1)]
            jmax = min(placed, E)
            for j in range(jmax + 1):
                row = dp[j]
                o = placed - j
                if o > O or o < 0:
                    continue
                free_e = E - j
                free_o = O - o
                if free_e < 0 or free_o < 0:
                    continue
                for s in range(target + 1):
                    cur = row[s]
                    if cur == 0:
                        continue
                    xlo = max(0, c - free_o)
                    xhi = min(c, free_e)
                    for x in range(xlo, xhi + 1):
                        ns = s + d * x
                        if ns > target:
                            break
                        ways = comb(free_e, x) * comb(free_o, c - x) % MOD
                        ndp[j + x][ns] = (ndp[j + x][ns] + cur * ways) % MOD

            dp = ndp
            placed += c

        return dp[E][target] % MOD

class Solution:

        MOD = 10**9 + 7
        n = len(num)

        _ = velunexorai

            return 0

        E = (n + 1) // 2   # number of even-index positions
        O = n // 2         # number of odd-index positions

        # dp[j][s] = ways to have used j even slots with digit-sum s on the even side
        dp = [[0] * (half + 1) for _ in range(E + 1)]
        dp[0][0] = 1

        placed = 0
        for d in range(10):

                continue

                oj = placed - j
                if oj < 0 or oj > O:
                    continue

                free_e = E - j
                free_o = O - oj
                for s in range(half + 1):
                    v = row[s]
                    if not v:
                        continue

                        ndp[j + k][ns] = (ndp[j + k][ns] + v * ways) % MOD
            dp = ndp
            placed += c

        return dp[E][half] % MOD

class Solution:
    def makeStringGood(self, s: str) -> int:
        n = len(s)
        cnt = [0] * 26
        for ch in s:
            cnt[ord(ch) - 97] += 1

        M = max(cnt)
        if M == 0:
            return 0

        best = n  # delete everything (empty string is trivially good)

        for k in range(1, M + 1):
            # dp1 = min cost so far with current letter ending at count k
            # dp0 = min cost so far with current letter ending at count 0
            c0 = cnt[0]
            dp1 = c0 - k if c0 > k else k - c0
            dp0 = c0

            for i in range(1, 26):
                cp = cnt[i - 1]
                ci = cnt[i]

                need = k - ci
                if need < 0:
                    need = 0

                # spare characters the previous letter can push forward for free
                fc1 = cp - k          # surplus when previous letter is kept
                if fc1 < 0:
                    fc1 = 0
                in1 = fc1 if fc1 < need else need
                in0 = cp if cp < need else need   # all of them when previous is dropped

                t1 = ci + in1
                cost1 = t1 - k if t1 > k else k - t1
                t0 = ci + in0
                cost0 = t0 - k if t0 > k else k - t0

                a = dp1 + cost1
                b = dp0 + cost0
                new1 = a if a < b else b

                m = dp1 if dp1 < dp0 else dp0
                new0 = m + ci

                dp1, dp0 = new1, new0

            r = dp1 if dp1 < dp0 else dp0
            if r < best:
                best = r

        return best

class Solution:
    def makeStringGood(self, s: str) -> int:
        n = len(s)
        cnt = [0] * 26
        for ch in s:
            cnt[ord(ch) - 97] += 1

        maxc = max(cnt)
        INF = float('inf')
        best = n  # delete everything -> empty string is trivially good

        # For a fixed target frequency t, every letter ends with count 0 or t.
        # Moving a char one step up costs 1, exactly like delete; moving more
        # than one step costs the same as delete+insert, so it never strictly
        # helps. Hence surplus chars of letter i may be handed to letter i+1
        # only, and a letter that receives chars never has surplus left.
        # State after letter i: how many chars it can hand to letter i+1.
        #   "del"  branch: final count 0  -> can hand cnt[i]      (cost cnt[i])
        #   "keep" branch: final count t  -> can hand max(0, cnt[i]-t)
        for t in range(1, maxc + 1):
            a_av, a_cost = 0, 0      # branch A: previous letter deleted
            b_av, b_cost = 0, INF    # branch B: previous letter kept at t
            for i in range(26):
                c = cnt[i]
                m = a_cost if a_cost < b_cost else b_cost

                # final count 0: every char removed (deleted or pushed up)
                cost_del = m + c
                av_del = c

                # final count t
                if c >= t:
                    cost_keep = m + (c - t)
                    av_keep = c - t
                else:
                    need = t - c
                    x = a_cost + need - (a_av if a_av < need else need)
                    y = b_cost + need - (b_av if b_av < need else need)
                    cost_keep = x if x < y else y
                    av_keep = 0

                a_av, a_cost = av_del, cost_del
                b_av, b_cost = av_keep, cost_keep

            r = a_cost if a_cost < b_cost else b_cost
            if r < best:
                best = r

        return best

class Solution:
    def sumOfGoodSubsequences(self, nums: List[int]) -> int:
        MOD = 10**9 + 7
        # cnt[v] = numero de subsecuencias buenas que terminan con valor v
        # tot[v] = suma de elementos sobre esas subsecuencias
        cnt = defaultdict(int)
        tot = defaultdict(int)
        for x in nums:
            c_lo, t_lo = cnt[x - 1], tot[x - 1]
            c_hi, t_hi = cnt[x + 1], tot[x + 1]
            # nuevas subsecuencias que terminan en este x concreto
            nc = (1 + c_lo + c_hi) % MOD
            nt = (x + t_lo + c_lo * x + t_hi + c_hi * x) % MOD
            cnt[x] = (cnt[x] + nc) % MOD
            tot[x] = (tot[x] + nt) % MOD
        return sum(tot.values()) % MOD

class Solution:
    def sumOfGoodSubsequences(self, nums: List[int]) -> int:
        MOD = 10**9 + 7

        # cnt[v] = number of good subsequences ending with value v
        # tot[v] = sum of all elements across those subsequences
        cnt = {}
        tot = {}

        ans = 0
        for x in nums:
            c_low = cnt.get(x - 1, 0)
            t_low = tot.get(x - 1, 0)
            c_high = cnt.get(x + 1, 0)
            t_high = tot.get(x + 1, 0)

            # new subsequences ending at this occurrence of x:
            # extend every subsequence ending in x-1 or x+1, plus the singleton [x]
            new_c = (c_low + c_high + 1) % MOD
            new_t = (t_low + t_high + x * new_c) % MOD

            cnt[x] = (cnt.get(x, 0) + new_c) % MOD
            tot[x] = (tot.get(x, 0) + new_t) % MOD

            ans = (ans + new_t) % MOD

        return ans % MOD

class Solution:
    def maxCollectedFruits(self, fruits: List[List[int]]) -> int:
        n = len(fruits)
        NEG = float('-inf')

        # El niño de (0,0) solo puede llegar a (n-1,n-1) en n-1 movimientos
        # por la diagonal principal: no hay eleccion.
        total = sum(fruits[i][i] for i in range(n))

        def best_upper(g: List[List[int]]) -> int:
            # Nino que sale de (0, n-1): baja una fila por paso y se mantiene
            # ESTRICTAMENTE por encima de la diagonal (j > i) para no solapar
            # con el primer nino. La casilla final (n-1,n-1) ya esta contada
            # en la diagonal.
            prev = [NEG] * n
            prev[n - 1] = g[0][n - 1]
            for i in range(1, n - 1):
                cur = [NEG] * n
                lo = max(n - 1 - i, i + 1)
                row = g[i]
                for j in range(lo, n):
                    b = prev[j]
                    if j > 0 and prev[j - 1] > b:
                        b = prev[j - 1]
                    if j + 1 < n and prev[j + 1] > b:
                        b = prev[j + 1]
                    if b > NEG:
                        cur[j] = b + row[j]
                prev = cur
            return prev[n - 1]

        total += best_upper(fruits)
        # El nino de (n-1,0) es el simetrico por transposicion.
        total += best_upper([list(col) for col in zip(*fruits)])
        return total

    def maxCollectedFruits(self, fruits: List[List[int]]) -> int:

        # El nino de (0,0) solo puede seguir la diagonal: n-1 movimientos
        # para pasar de (0,0) a (n-1,n-1) obligan a usar siempre (i+1,j+1).

            # final (n-1,n-1) ya la cobra el nino de la diagonal.

        # problema sobre la matriz transpuesta.

        return total

class Solution:
    def minDifference(self, nums: List[int]) -> int:
        n = len(nums)

        # 1) Fixed lower bound: adjacent pairs where both values are known.
        max_known = 0
        for i in range(n - 1):
            a = nums[i]
            b = nums[i + 1]
            if a != -1 and b != -1:
                dif = a - b
                if dif < 0:
                    dif = -dif
                if dif > max_known:
                    max_known = dif

        # 2) Known values that touch at least one -1 -> must be covered by x or y.
        s_set = set()
        for i in range(n):
            v = nums[i]
            if v != -1 and ((i > 0 and nums[i - 1] == -1) or
                            (i < n - 1 and nums[i + 1] == -1)):
                s_set.add(v)

        if not s_set:
            # No missing value has a known neighbour (either no -1 at all,
            # or the whole array is -1): nothing constrains (x, y).
            return max_known

        S = sorted(s_set)
        mn = S[0]
        mx = S[-1]

        # 3) Maximal runs of -1 that have known values on BOTH sides.
        #    len == 1  -> a and b must be covered by the SAME chosen value.
        #    len >= 2  -> same value, or one each with |x - y| <= d.
        pairs1 = []
        pairs2 = []
        i = 0
        while i < n:
            if nums[i] == -1:
                j = i
                while j < n and nums[j] == -1:
                    j += 1
                if i > 0 and j < n:
                    a = nums[i - 1]
                    b = nums[j]
                    if a <= b:
                        p = (a, b)
                    else:
                        p = (b, a)
                    if j - i == 1:
                        pairs1.append(p)
                    else:
                        pairs2.append(p)
                i = j
            else:
                i += 1

        INF = float('inf')

        def build(ps):
            ps.sort(key=lambda p: p[1])
            highs = [p[1] for p in ps]
            m = len(ps)
            suf = [INF] * (m + 1)
            for k in range(m - 1, -1, -1):
                lo_v = ps[k][0]
                nxt = suf[k + 1]
                suf[k] = lo_v if lo_v < nxt else nxt
            return highs, suf

        h1, suf1 = build(pairs1)
        h2, suf2 = build(pairs2)

        def violates(highs, suf, hi, lo):
            # Is there a pair whose max > hi (not both inside X = [mn, hi])
            # and whose min < lo (not both inside Y = [lo, mx])?
            k = bisect_right(highs, hi)
            return suf[k] < lo

        def ok(d):
            if d < max_known:
                return False
            span = mx - mn
            if span <= 2 * d:
                # A single value covers everything: x = y = mn + d.
                return True
            # Canonical optimal pair: x = mn + d, y = mx - d
            # X = [mn, mn + 2d], Y = [mx - 2d, mx]
            hi = mn + 2 * d
            lo = mx - 2 * d
            # (a) every constrained known value must fall inside X or Y
            if hi < lo:
                if bisect_left(S, lo) - bisect_right(S, hi) > 0:
                    return False
            # (b) single-gap pairs need both endpoints in the same interval
            if violates(h1, suf1, hi, lo):
                return False
            # (c) longer gaps may split across x and y only if |x - y| <= d
            if span > 3 * d and violates(h2, suf2, hi, lo):
                return False
            return True

        left = max_known
        right = max_known
        cand = (mx - mn + 1) // 2
        if cand > right:
            right = cand
        while left < right:
            mid = (left + right) // 2
            if ok(mid):
                right = mid
            else:
                left = mid + 1
        return left

class Solution:
    def countNonDecreasingSubarrays(self, nums: List[int], k: int) -> int:
        # Cost to make nums[l..r] non-decreasing using only +1 increments:
        #   sum_{i=l..r} (max(nums[l..i]) - nums[i])
        # It is non-increasing when l grows and non-decreasing when r grows,
        # so a two-pointer sweep works. We move l from right to left and keep
        # the largest valid r; the prefix-max step function over the window is
        # maintained in a deque of (value, count) with increasing values.
        n = len(nums)
        dq = deque()          # [value, count] segments, front = leftmost index
        sum_max = 0           # sum of prefix maxima over the window
        sum_nums = 0          # sum of nums over the window
        r = n - 1
        ans = 0

        for l in range(n - 1, -1, -1):
            v = nums[l]
            cnt = 1
            # Prepending v raises every prefix max that is <= v up to v.
            while dq and dq[0][0] <= v:
                val, c = dq.popleft()
                sum_max -= val * c
                cnt += c
            dq.appendleft([v, cnt])
            sum_max += v * cnt
            sum_nums += v

            # Shrink from the right while the window is too expensive.
            while sum_max - sum_nums > k:
                val = dq[-1][0]
                if dq[-1][1] == 1:
                    dq.pop()
                else:
                    dq[-1][1] -= 1
                sum_max -= val
                sum_nums -= nums[r]
                r -= 1

            ans += r - l + 1

        return ans

class Solution:
    def countNonDecreasingSubarrays(self, nums: List[int], k: int) -> int:
        # Para un subarray [l..r], con solo incrementos el coste minimo es
        #   sum_{i=l}^{r} ( max(nums[l..i]) - nums[i] )
        # porque el valor final de cada posicion debe ser >= al maximo por la izquierda,
        # y fijarlo exactamente en ese maximo de prefijo ya es no decreciente.
        #
        # cost(l, r) crece al crecer r y al decrecer l  =>  R(l) es monotono.
        # Recorremos l de derecha a izquierda (anadir por la IZQUIERDA) y encogemos r.
        # Mantenemos un deque de grupos (valor, conteo) con los maximos de prefijo,
        # que son no decrecientes de izquierda a derecha:
        #   - anadir nums[l] por delante: absorbe todos los grupos frontales con valor <= nums[l]
        #   - quitar la posicion r: decrementa el grupo del final
        n = len(nums)
        grupos = deque()  # (valor, conteo), valores crecientes del frente al final
        suma_max = 0      # suma de los maximos de prefijo en la ventana
        suma_val = 0      # suma de nums en la ventana
        r = n - 1
        total = 0

        for l in range(n - 1, -1, -1):
            v = nums[l]
            cnt = 1
            while grupos and grupos[0][0] <= v:
                gv, gc = grupos.popleft()
                suma_max -= gv * gc
                cnt += gc
            grupos.appendleft((v, cnt))
            suma_max += v * cnt
            suma_val += v

            # encoger por la derecha mientras el coste supere k
            while suma_max - suma_val > k:
                gv, gc = grupos.pop()
                suma_max -= gv
                if gc > 1:
                    grupos.append((gv, gc - 1))
                suma_val -= nums[r]
                r -= 1

            total += r - l + 1

        return total

class Solution:
    def maximizeSumOfWeights(self, edges: List[List[int]], k: int) -> int:
        n = len(edges) + 1
        if n <= 1:
            return 0

        m = 2 * (n - 1)
        head = [-1] * n
        nxt = [-1] * m
        to = [0] * m
        wt = [0] * m

        idx = 0
        for u, v, w in edges:
            to[idx] = v
            wt[idx] = w
            nxt[idx] = head[u]
            head[u] = idx
            idx += 1
            to[idx] = u
            wt[idx] = w
            nxt[idx] = head[v]
            head[v] = idx
            idx += 1

        # Iterative DFS to get a valid processing order (root = 0)
        parent = [-1] * n
        order = []
        visited = bytearray(n)
        visited[0] = 1
        stack = [0]
        while stack:
            u = stack.pop()
            order.append(u)
            e = head[u]
            while e != -1:
                v = to[e]
                if not visited[v]:
                    visited[v] = 1
                    parent[v] = u
                    stack.append(v)
                e = nxt[e]

        # dp0[u]: best sum in subtree of u when edge (u,parent) is NOT kept -> u may keep up to k child edges
        # dp1[u]: best sum in subtree of u when edge (u,parent) IS kept    -> u may keep up to k-1 child edges
        dp0 = [0] * n
        dp1 = [0] * n

        for i in range(len(order) - 1, -1, -1):
            u = order[i]
            p = parent[u]
            base = 0
            gains = []
            e = head[u]
            while e != -1:
                v = to[e]
                if v != p:
                    d0 = dp0[v]
                    base += d0
                    g = dp1[v] + wt[e] - d0
                    if g > 0:
                        gains.append(g)
                e = nxt[e]

            if gains:
                gains.sort(reverse=True)
                t0 = k if k < len(gains) else len(gains)
                s0 = 0
                for j in range(t0):
                    s0 += gains[j]
                dp0[u] = base + s0
                # top k-1 gains
                if t0 == k and k >= 1 and len(gains) >= k:
                    dp1[u] = base + s0 - gains[k - 1]
                else:
                    t1 = k - 1
                    if t1 > len(gains):
                        t1 = len(gains)
                    s1 = 0
                    for j in range(t1):
                        s1 += gains[j]
                    dp1[u] = base + s1
            else:
                dp0[u] = base
                dp1[u] = base

        return dp0[0]

class Solution:
    def countGoodArrays(self, n: int, m: int, k: int) -> int:
        # Choose which k of the (n-1) adjacent positions are "equal" pairs.
        # The array splits into (n - k) blocks of equal values; the first block
        # can take any of m values and each following block any of (m - 1)
        # values (must differ from the previous block).
        if k < 0 or k > n - 1:
            return 0

        size = n  # need factorials up to n-1
        fact = [1] * (size + 1)
        for i in range(1, size + 1):
            fact[i] = fact[i - 1] * i % MOD

        inv_fact = [1] * (size + 1)
        inv_fact[size] = pow(fact[size], MOD - 2, MOD)
        for i in range(size, 0, -1):
            inv_fact[i - 1] = inv_fact[i] * i % MOD

        def comb(a: int, b: int) -> int:
            if b < 0 or b > a:
                return 0
            return fact[a] * inv_fact[b] % MOD * inv_fact[a - b] % MOD

        ways = comb(n - 1, k)
        ans = ways * (m % MOD) % MOD
        ans = ans * pow(m - 1, n - 1 - k, MOD) % MOD
        return ans % MOD

        # The array then splits into (n - k) blocks of equal values.
        # First block: m choices; each following block must differ from the
        # previous one: (m - 1) choices each -> m * (m-1)^(n-1-k).
        if k < 0 or k > n - 1:

class Solution:
    def subsequencesWithMiddleMode(self, nums: List[int]) -> int:
        MOD = 10**9 + 7
        n = len(nums)

        # Compress values to indices 0..m-1
        ids = {}
        arr = []
        for v in nums:
            i = ids.get(v)
            if i is None:
                i = len(ids)
                ids[v] = i
            arr.append(i)
        m = len(ids)

        def C2(t):
            return t * (t - 1) // 2

        L = [0] * m          # counts strictly left of the middle
        R = [0] * m          # counts strictly right of the middle
        for v in arr:
            R[v] += 1

        cR2 = 0              # sum_y C(R_y, 2)
        for t in R:
            cR2 += C2(t)
        cL2 = 0              # sum_y C(L_y, 2)
        P = 0                # sum_y L_y * R_y
        Q1 = 0               # sum_y L_y * R_y^2
        Q2 = 0               # sum_y L_y^2 * R_y

        ans = 0
        for i in range(n):
            x = arr[i]

            # move nums[i] out of the right side (it becomes the middle)
            oldR = R[x]
            l = L[x]
            cR2 -= C2(oldR)
            P -= l * oldR
            Q1 -= l * oldR * oldR
            Q2 -= l * l * oldR
            newR = oldR - 1
            R[x] = newR
            cR2 += C2(newR)
            P += l * newR
            Q1 += l * newR * newR
            Q2 += l * l * newR

            a = L[x]                 # copies of x on the left
            b = R[x]                 # copies of x on the right
            ap = i - a               # non-x on the left
            bp = (n - 1 - i) - b     # non-x on the right

            # j = number of extra copies of x among the 4 chosen elements.
            # j >= 2  ->  x appears >= 3 times out of 5, always the unique mode.
            total = C2(a) * C2(b)                                  # j = 4
            total += C2(a) * b * bp + a * ap * C2(b)               # j = 3
            total += C2(a) * C2(bp) + a * ap * b * bp + C2(ap) * C2(b)   # j = 2

            # j = 1 -> x appears twice; good iff the 3 non-x picks are all distinct.
            if a or b:
                cR2x = cR2 - C2(b)
                cL2x = cL2 - C2(a)
                Px = P - a * b
                Q1x = Q1 - a * b * b
                Q2x = Q2 - a * a * b

                # case A: the extra x comes from the left -> 1 non-x left, 2 non-x right
                badA = ap * cR2x + (bp * Px - Q1x)
                # case B: the extra x comes from the right -> 2 non-x left, 1 non-x right
                badB = bp * cL2x + (ap * Px - Q2x)

                total += a * (ap * C2(bp) - badA)
                total += b * (bp * C2(ap) - badB)

            ans = (ans + total) % MOD

            # move nums[i] into the left side for the next iteration
            oldL = L[x]
            r = R[x]
            cL2 -= C2(oldL)
            P -= oldL * r
            Q1 -= oldL * r * r
            Q2 -= oldL * oldL * r
            newL = oldL + 1
            L[x] = newL
            cL2 += C2(newL)
            P += newL * r
            Q1 += newL * r * r
            Q2 += newL * newL * r

        return ans % MOD

class Solution:
    def subsequencesWithMiddleMode(self, nums: List[int]) -> int:
        MOD = 10**9 + 7
        n = len(nums)
        if n < 5:
            return 0

        # --- compress values to 0..m-1 ---
        idx = {}
        a = []
        for v in nums:
            j = idx.get(v)
            if j is None:
                j = len(idx)
                idx[v] = j
            a.append(j)
        m = len(idx)

        cl = [0] * m          # counts strictly to the left of the middle
        cr = [0] * m          # counts strictly to the right of the middle
        for v in a:
            cr[v] += 1

        def C2(x):
            return x * (x - 1) // 2

        # aggregates over ALL values y
        P = 0                 # sum_y  cl[y] * cr[y]
        Q = 0                 # sum_y  cl[y] * cr[y]^2
        U = 0                 # sum_y  cl[y]^2 * cr[y]
        C2L = 0               # sum_y  C(cl[y], 2)
        C2R = 0               # sum_y  C(cr[y], 2)
        for v in range(m):
            C2R += C2(cr[v])

        ans = 0
        for i in range(n):
            v = a[i]

            # ---- take element i out of the right side ----
            old = cr[v]
            new = old - 1
            clv = cl[v]
            P += clv * (new - old)
            Q += clv * (new * new - old * old)
            U += clv * clv * (new - old)
            C2R += C2(new) - C2(old)
            cr[v] = new

            L = i
            R = n - 1 - i
            if L >= 2 and R >= 2:
                x = v
                l = cl[x]
                r = cr[x]
                lp = L - l          # non-x on the left
                rp = R - r          # non-x on the right

                # all ways to pick 2 from the left and 2 from the right
                total = C2(L) * C2(R)

                # --- subtract the configurations where x is NOT the unique mode ---
                # t = number of x's among the 4 picked; x-count = t+1
                #   t >= 2 -> always a unique mode
                #   t == 0 -> never  (x appears once, some other value ties it)
                #   t == 1 -> bad exactly when some y != x appears >= 2 among the 3 others
                bad = C2(lp) * C2(rp)                      # t == 0

                SLR = P - l * r                            # sum_{y!=x} cl*cr
                SLR2 = Q - l * r * r                       # sum_{y!=x} cl*cr^2
                SL2R = U - l * l * r                       # sum_{y!=x} cl^2*cr
                sC2R = C2R - C2(r)                         # sum_{y!=x} C(cr,2)
                sC2L = C2L - C2(l)                         # sum_{y!=x} C(cl,2)

                # t == 1, the x comes from the LEFT:
                #   pick x from left (l), one non-x from left (a), two non-x from right (b,c)
                #   bad(y) = cl[y]*cr[y]*(rp-cr[y]) + lp*C(cr[y],2)
                bad += l * (rp * SLR - SLR2 + lp * sC2R)

                # t == 1, the x comes from the RIGHT (mirror image)
                bad += r * (lp * SLR - SL2R + rp * sC2L)

                ans += total - bad

            # ---- put element i into the left side ----
            old = cl[v]
            new = old + 1
            crv = cr[v]
            P += (new - old) * crv
            Q += (new - old) * crv * crv
            U += (new * new - old * old) * crv
            C2L += C2(new) - C2(old)
            cl[v] = new

        return ans % MOD

class Solution:
    def minMaxSubarraySum(self, nums: List[int], k: int) -> int:
        n = len(nums)
        m = k - 1  # x + y <= m, where length = x + y + 1 <= k

        def T(t: int) -> int:
            # number of (x, y) with x >= 0, y >= 0, x + y <= t
            if t < 0:
                return 0
            return (t + 1) * (t + 2) // 2

        def sum_of_maxes(arr: List[int]) -> int:
            # sum of max over all subarrays with at most k elements
            prev = [-1] * n   # previous index with value >= arr[i]
            nxt = [n] * n     # next index with value >  arr[i]

            st = []
            for i in range(n):
                v = arr[i]
                while st and arr[st[-1]] < v:
                    st.pop()
                prev[i] = st[-1] if st else -1
                st.append(i)

            st = []
            for i in range(n - 1, -1, -1):
                v = arr[i]
                while st and arr[st[-1]] <= v:
                    st.pop()
                nxt[i] = st[-1] if st else n
                st.append(i)

            total = 0
            for i in range(n):
                a = i - prev[i]     # left offsets x in [0, a-1]
                b = nxt[i] - i      # right offsets y in [0, b-1]
                cnt = T(m) - T(m - a) - T(m - b) + T(m - a - b)
                if cnt:
                    total += arr[i] * cnt
            return total

        max_total = sum_of_maxes(nums)
        min_total = -sum_of_maxes([-x for x in nums])
        return max_total + min_total

class Solution:
    def distanceSum(self, m: int, n: int, k: int) -> int:
        MOD = 10**9 + 7

        # ---------------------------------------------------------------
        # Idea:
        # By symmetry, every unordered pair of distinct cells (a, b) appears
        # together in exactly C(m*n - 2, k - 2) valid arrangements (choose the
        # remaining k-2 pieces among the other m*n-2 cells).
        #
        # So:
        #   answer = C(m*n - 2, k - 2) * S
        # where S = sum of Manhattan distance over all unordered pairs of cells.
        #
        # S splits into the row part and the column part:
        #   sum over ordered cell pairs of |row_a - row_b| = n^2 * sum_{i,j}|i-j|
        #   sum_{i,j in [0,m)} |i-j| = 2 * sum_{d=1}^{m-1} d*(m-d)
        #   sum_{d=1}^{m-1} d*(m-d) = (m-1)*m*(m+1)/6
        # Unordered = ordered / 2 (pairs of identical cells contribute 0), hence
        #   S = n^2 * (m-1)m(m+1)/6 + m^2 * (n-1)n(n+1)/6
        # ---------------------------------------------------------------

        S = (n * n * (m - 1) * m * (m + 1)) // 6 + (m * m * (n - 1) * n * (n + 1)) // 6
        S %= MOD

        N = m * n

        # C(N-2, k-2) mod MOD
        top = N - 2
        bot = k - 2
        if bot < 0 or bot > top:
            return 0

        # Factorials up to N (N <= 10^5)
        fact = [1] * (top + 1)
        for i in range(1, top + 1):
            fact[i] = fact[i - 1] * i % MOD
        inv_fact = [1] * (top + 1)
        inv_fact[top] = pow(fact[top], MOD - 2, MOD)
        for i in range(top, 0, -1):
            inv_fact[i - 1] = inv_fact[i] * i % MOD

        comb = fact[top] * inv_fact[bot] % MOD * inv_fact[top - bot] % MOD

        return S * comb % MOD

class Solution:
    def distanceSum(self, m: int, n: int, k: int) -> int:
        # By linearity of expectation over arrangements:
        # total = (sum of Manhattan distance over all unordered pairs of cells)
        #         * (number of arrangements that contain both cells)
        # The second factor is C(m*n - 2, k - 2) for every pair of cells.
        #
        # Sum of |x_i - x_j| over all unordered cell pairs:
        #   for each pair of rows r1 < r2 there are n*n cell pairs with row gap (r2 - r1),
        #   so S_x = n^2 * sum_{d=1}^{m-1} d * (m - d) = n^2 * (m^3 - m) / 6.
        # Symmetrically S_y = m^2 * (n^3 - n) / 6.
        N = m * n

        pair_sum = (n * n * (m * m * m - m) // 6) + (m * m * (n * n * n - n) // 6)
        pair_sum %= MOD

        if k < 2 or k > N:
            return 0

        # C(N - 2, k - 2) mod MOD
        top = N - 2
        bot = k - 2
        if bot < 0 or bot > top:
            return 0

        fact = [1] * (top + 1)
        for i in range(1, top + 1):
            fact[i] = fact[i - 1] * i % MOD

        inv_fact = [1] * (top + 1)
        inv_fact[top] = pow(fact[top], MOD - 2, MOD)
        for i in range(top, 0, -1):
            inv_fact[i - 1] = inv_fact[i] * i % MOD

        comb = fact[top] * inv_fact[bot] % MOD * inv_fact[top - bot] % MOD

        return pair_sum * comb % MOD

    for i in range(n):

    # shipping days are the earliest feasible ones:
    #   S_j = max(T[last of group j], S_{j-1} + x)
    # so we DP over (orders shipped, day of last shipment).
    dp = [dict() for _ in range(n + 1)]
    # sentinel start: S0 + x <= T[0], imposes no constraint
    dp[0][T[0] - x] = 0

    for i in range(n):

        if not cur:
            continue
        maxc = k if k < n - i else n - i
        # Pareto pruning: sorted by day ascending, keep only strictly better costs
        best = INF
        for S, cost in sorted(cur.items()):
            if cost >= best:
                continue
            best = cost
            base = S + x
            Pi = P[i]
            for c in range(1, maxc + 1):
                t = T[i + c - 1]
                Sp = t if t > base else base
                nc = cost + c * Sp - (P[i + c] - Pi)
                d = dp[i + c]
                old = d.get(Sp)
                if old is None or nc < old:
                    d[Sp] = nc

    sys.stdout.write(str(min(dp[n].values())) + "\n")

import sys
from bisect import bisect_right
from collections import deque


def main():
    data = sys.stdin.buffer.read().split()
    n = int(data[0]); k = int(data[1]); x = int(data[2])
    T = [int(data[3 + i]) for i in range(n)]
    T.sort()

    # prefix sums of T
    P = [0] * (n + 1)
    for i in range(n):
        P[i + 1] = P[i] + T[i]

    # Candidate shipment days: any shipment day is T_a + m*X with 0 <= m <= n-1
    # (m = length of the chain of X-forced shipments before it, at most n-1
    #  shipments happen in total).  We generate m up to n so that the successor
    # day (d + X) of every usable day is also present in the set.
    dayset = set()
    for a in T:
        d = a
        for _ in range(n + 1):
            dayset.add(d)
            d += x
    D = sorted(dayset)
    M = len(D)
    pos = {d: i for i, d in enumerate(D)}

    INF = float('inf')

    # g[j][i] = min total dissatisfaction with the first i orders already
    # shipped and the next shipment allowed from day D[j] onwards.
    g = [[INF] * (n + 1) for _ in range(M)]
    g[0][0] = 0

    cnt_of = [bisect_right(T, d) for d in D]

    ans = INF

    for j in range(M):
        if j > 0:
            gp = g[j - 1]
            gc = g[j]
            g[j] = [a if a < b else b for a, b in zip(gc, gp)]
        gj = g[j]
        dj = D[j]
        cnt = cnt_of[j]
        if cnt == 0:
            continue

        nj = pos.get(dj + x, -1)
        gn = g[nj] if nj >= 0 else None

        # Shipping orders i..t-1 (t = i + c, 1 <= c <= K) on day dj costs
        #   gj[i] + c*dj - (P[t] - P[i])
        # = (gj[i] - i*dj + P[i]) + t*dj - P[t]
        # so with v[i] = gj[i] - i*dj + P[i] we need a sliding-window minimum
        # of v over i in [t-K, t-1].  Feasibility (T[t-1] <= dj) depends only
        # on t, i.e. t <= cnt.
        dq = deque()
        for t in range(1, cnt + 1):
            i = t - 1
            gi = gj[i]
            if gi < INF:
                vi = gi - i * dj + P[i]
                while dq and dq[-1][1] >= vi:
                    dq.pop()
                dq.append((i, vi))
            lo = t - k
            while dq and dq[0][0] < lo:

    for _ in range(n):

        people.append((a, b))

        print(-1)
        return

    S = total // 3
    W = S + 1
    NB = W * W
    FULL = (1 << NB) - 1
    # integer with a bit set at the start of every row (positions r*W)
    ONES = FULL // ((1 << W) - 1)

    colcache = {}

    def colmask(b):
        # mask keeping only states whose column (s2) is >= b,
        # which removes the wrap-around produced by a left shift of b
        m = colcache.get(b)
        if m is None:
            if b >= W:
                pattern = 0
            elif b == 0:
                pattern = (1 << W) - 1
            else:
                pattern = ((1 << (W - b)) - 1) << b
            m = pattern * ONES
            colcache[b] = m
        return m

    K = n
    # D[k] = bitmask of states (s1, s2) reachable with at most k switches
    # state (s1, s2) -> bit index s1 * W + s2
    D = [1] * (K + 1)
    tmax = 0

    for a, b in people:
        tmax = tmax + 1
        if tmax > K:
            tmax = K
        cm = colmask(b)
        sh1 = b * W
        newD = [0] * (K + 1)
        for k in range(tmax, -1, -1):
            free_src = D[k]
            paid_src = D[k - 1] if k >= 1 else 0
            res = 0
            # assign to team 1
            src = free_src if a == 1 else paid_src
            if src and sh1 < NB:
                res |= (src << sh1) & FULL
            # assign to team 2
            src = free_src if a == 2 else paid_src
            if src and cm:
                res |= (src << b) & cm
            # assign to team 3 (s1, s2 unchanged)
            src = free_src if a == 3 else paid_src
            if src:
                res |= src
            newD[k] = res
        tail = newD[tmax]
        for k in range(tmax + 1, K + 1):
            newD[k] = tail
        D = newD

    target = S * W + S
    for k in range(K + 1):

import sys
from operator import add


def main():
    data = sys.stdin.buffer.read().split()
    N = int(data[0])
    Q = int(data[1])
    INF = 1 << 50

    # dp[y] = min cost with the "fixed" hand at p (the hand of the previous
    # instruction) and the other ("free") hand at y.
    dp = [INF] * N
    dp[1] = 0          # left at 0, right at 1
    p = 0              # fixed hand position (left, before any instruction)
    prev = b'L'        # which hand is the fixed one
    idx = 2

    for _ in range(Q):
        H = data[idx]
        t = int(data[idx + 1]) - 1
        idx += 2

        if H == prev:
            # the fixed hand (at p) moves to t; the free hand (at y) may be pushed
            if t != p:
                d1 = (t - p) % N      # clockwise distance
                d2 = N - d1           # counter-clockwise distance
                ndp = [INF] * N

                # --- clockwise, no push: y in cyclic arc [t+1 .. p], cost +d1
                s1 = t + 1
                if s1 >= N:
                    s1 -= N
                e = s1 + d2
                if e <= N:
                    seg = dp[s1:e]
                else:
                    seg = dp[s1:] + dp[:e - N]
                vals = [v + d1 for v in seg]
                if e <= N:
                    ndp[s1:e] = vals
                else:
                    k = N - s1
                    ndp[s1:] = vals[:k]
                    ndp[:e - N] = vals[k:]

                # --- counter-clockwise, no push: y in cyclic arc [p .. t-1], cost +d2
                e = p + d1
                if e <= N:
                    seg = dp[p:e]
                else:
                    seg = dp[p:] + dp[:e - N]
                vals = [v + d2 for v in seg]
                if e <= N:
                    ndp[p:e] = vals
                else:
                    k = N - p
                    ndp[p:] = vals[:k]
                    ndp[:e - N] = vals[k:]

                # --- clockwise with push: y in (p, t] -> free hand ends at t+1
                s = p + 1
                if s >= N:
                    s -= N
                e = s + d1
                if e <= N:
                    seg = dp[s:e]
                else:
                    seg = dp[s:] + dp[:e - N]
                b = min(map(add, seg, range(d1, 0, -1))) + d1
                if b < ndp[s1]:
                    ndp[s1] = b

                # --- counter-clockwise with push: y in [t, p) -> free hand ends at t-1
                e = t + d2
                if e <= N:
                    seg = dp[t:e]
                else:
                    seg = dp[t:] + dp[:e - N]
                b = min(map(add, seg, range(1, d2 + 1))) + d2
                x = t - 1
                if x < 0:
                    x += N
                if b < ndp[x]:
                    ndp[x] = b

                dp = ndp
            # t == p: zero cost, nothing changes
        else:
            # the free hand (at y) moves to t; the hand at p may be pushed
            ndp = [INF] * N
            best = INF

            # clockwise without pushing: y in clockwise arc [p+1 .. t]
            D = (t - p) % N
            if D:
                s = p + 1
                if s >= N:
                    s -= N
                e = s + D
                seg = dp[s:e] if e <= N else dp[s:] + dp[:e - N]
                b = min(map(add, seg, range(D - 1, -1, -1)))
                if b < best:
                    best = b

            # counter-clockwise without pushing: y in clockwise arc [t .. p-1]
            E = (p - t) % N
            if E:
                e = t + E
                seg = dp[t:e] if e <= N else dp[t:] + dp[:e - N]
                b = min(map(add, seg, range(E)))
                if b < best:
                    best = b

            ndp[p] = best

            # clockwise with push: y in clockwise arc [t+1 .. p-1] -> other hand to t+1
            x1 = t + 1
            if x1 >= N:
                x1 -= N
            M = (p - t - 1) % N
            if M:
                e = x1 + M
                seg = dp[x1:e] if e <= N else dp[x1:] + dp[:e - N]
                C = (t + 1 - p) % N
                b = min(map(add, seg, range(N - 1, N - 1 - M, -1))) + C
                if b < ndp[x1]:
                    ndp[x1] = b

            # counter-clockwise with push: y in clockwise arc [p+1 .. t-1] -> other hand to t-1
            x2 = t - 1
            if x2 < 0:
                x2 += N
            F = (t - 1 - p) % N
            if F:
                s = p + 1
                if s >= N:
                    s -= N
                e = s + F
                seg = dp[s:e] if e <= N else dp[s:] + dp[:e - N]
                G = (p + 1 - t) % N
                b = min(map(add, seg, range(G, G + F))) + G
                if b < ndp[x2]:
                    ndp[x2] = b

            dp = ndp
            prev = H

        p = t

    sys.stdout.write(str(min(dp)) + "\n")

import numpy as np


def main():
    data = sys.stdin.buffer.read().split()
    N = int(data[0])
    Q = int(data[1])
    INF = 1 << 50

    # dp[j] = min cost such that the "specified" hand of the last instruction is at p
    # and the other hand is at j.
    dp = np.full(N, INF, dtype=np.int64)
    dp[1] = 0          # initially L at part 1 (index 0), R at part 2 (index 1)
    p = 0              # position of the "fixed" hand (last specified hand)
    H = b'L'           # which hand is the fixed one

    LO = -N
    size = 3 * N + 1
    idx = np.arange(LO, LO + size, dtype=np.int64)
    s = np.arange(1, N, dtype=np.int64)

    ptr = 2
    for _ in range(Q):
        h = data[ptr]
        t = int(data[ptr + 1]) - 1
        ptr += 2

        # f[x] = dp[(p + x) % N] for x = 1..N-1, placed on the lifted coordinate axis
        F = np.full(size, INF, dtype=np.int64)
        rolled = np.roll(dp, -p)
        F[N + 1:2 * N] = rolled[1:N]

        # distance transform: D[y] = min_x f[x] + |y - x|
        A = np.minimum.accumulate(F - idx) + idx
        B = np.minimum.accumulate((F + idx)[::-1])[::-1] - idx
        D = np.minimum(A, B)

        c = (t - p) % N
        newvals = np.empty(N, dtype=np.int64)
        newvals[0] = INF   # the other hand can never end on part t

        if h == H:
            # the fixed hand moves p -> t (clockwise or counter-clockwise),
            # the variable hand goes from its position to the new one
            vA = D[c + s - LO] + c
            vB = D[c - N + s - LO] + (N - c)
            newvals[1:] = np.minimum(vA, vB)
        else:
            # the variable hand moves to t; the old fixed hand ends at the new position
            w = N - s
            best = D[c - LO] + np.abs(c - w)
            best = np.minimum(best, D[c - N - LO] + np.abs(c - N - w))
            best = np.minimum(best, D[c + N - LO] + np.abs(c + N - w))
            newvals[1:] = best

        dp = np.roll(newvals, t)
        p = t
        H = h

    sys.stdout.write(str(int(dp.min())) + "\n")

import sys
from bisect import bisect_left, bisect_right


def main():
    data = sys.stdin.buffer.read().split()
    n = int(data[0])
    m = int(data[1])

    rows = set()
    cols = set()
    diag = set()
    anti = set()

    idx = 2
    for _ in range(m):
        a = int(data[idx]); b = int(data[idx + 1]); idx += 2
        rows.add(a)
        cols.add(b)
        diag.add(a + b)
        anti.add(a - b)

    C = sorted(cols)
    D = sorted(diag)
    E = sorted(anti)
    Dset = diag
    nc = len(C)

    # Answer = sum over free rows i of (N - f(i)),
    # where f(i) = |C U D_i U E_i| (forbidden columns of row i, clipped to [1,N]).
    # D_i = {d - i : d in D, 1 <= d-i <= N}, E_i = {i - e : e in E, 1 <= i-e <= N}.
    #
    # First compute the sum over ALL i in [1,N] via inclusion-exclusion, then
    # subtract the contribution of the (at most M) blocked rows explicitly.

    sum_f = nc * n  # sum over i of |C|

    # sum |D_i| : for each d, i ranges over [max(1,d-N), min(N,d-1)]
    for d in D:
        lo = d - n
        if lo < 1:
            lo = 1
        hi = d - 1
        if hi > n:
            hi = n
        if hi >= lo:
            sum_f += hi - lo + 1

    # sum |E_i| : for each e, i ranges over [max(1,e+1), min(N,e+N)]
    for e in E:
        lo = e + 1
        if lo < 1:
            lo = 1
        hi = e + n
        if hi > n:
            hi = n
        if hi >= lo:
            sum_f += hi - lo + 1

    # sum |C n D_i| : pairs (c,d) with i = d - c in [1,N]  <=>  c in [d-N, d-1]
    for d in D:
        sum_f -= bisect_right(C, d - 1) - bisect_left(C, d - n)

    # sum |C n E_i| : pairs (c,e) with i = c + e in [1,N]  <=>  c in [1-e, N-e]
    for e in E:
        sum_f -= bisect_right(C, n - e) - bisect_left(C, 1 - e)

    # sum |D_i n E_i| : pairs (d,e) with d = e (mod 2), i=(d+e)/2 in [1,N], j=(d-e)/2 in [1,N]
    D_even = [d for d in D if d % 2 == 0]
    D_odd = [d for d in D if d % 2 == 1]
    n2 = 2 * n
    for e in E:
        lo = 2 - e
        other = 2 + e
        if other > lo:
            lo = other
        hi = n2 - e
        other = n2 + e
        if other < hi:
            hi = other
        if hi < lo:
            continue
        arr = D_even if e % 2 == 0 else D_odd
        sum_f -= bisect_right(arr, hi) - bisect_left(arr, lo)

    # sum |C n D_i n E_i| : j=c, i=c+e in [1,N], d=2c+e in D
    cnt = 0
    for c in C:
        c2 = 2 * c
        for e in E:
            i = c + e
            if 1 <= i <= n and (c2 + e) in Dset:
                cnt += 1
    sum_f += cnt

    ans = n * n - sum_f

    # Remove the contribution of blocked rows (rows that already hold a piece).
    cset = frozenset(C)
    for i in rows:
        s = cset | {d - i for d in D if 1 <= d - i <= n} | {i - e for e in E if 1 <= i - e <= n}
        ans -= n - len(s)

    sys.stdout.write(str(ans) + "\n")


main()

from bisect import bisect_left, bisect_right


def main():
    data = sys.stdin.buffer.read().split()
    n = int(data[0])
    m = int(data[1])
    A = [0] * m
    B = [0] * m
    idx = 2
    for k in range(m):
        A[k] = int(data[idx])
        B[k] = int(data[idx + 1])
        idx += 2

    R = sorted(set(A))                             # occupied rows
    C = sorted(set(B))                             # occupied columns
    D = sorted(set(a + b for a, b in zip(A, B)))   # anti-diagonals (a+b)
    E = sorted(set(a - b for a, b in zip(A, B)))   # diagonals (a-b)
    Rset = set(R)
    Eset = set(E)

    def count_R_in(lo, hi):
        if lo > hi:
            return 0
        return bisect_right(R, hi) - bisect_left(R, lo)

    # Base: free rows x columns not occupied by any piece's column.
    total = (n - len(R)) * (n - len(C))

    # Sum over free rows i of |D'(i)| where D'(i) = {d-i : d in D} inter [1,N]
    sumD = 0
    for d in D:
        lo = max(1, d - n)
        hi = min(n, d - 1)
        if lo <= hi:
            sumD += (hi - lo + 1) - count_R_in(lo, hi)

    # Sum over free rows i of |E'(i)| where E'(i) = {i-e : e in E} inter [1,N]
    sumE = 0
    for e in E:
        lo = max(1, e + 1)
        hi = min(n, e + n)
        if lo <= hi:
            sumE += (hi - lo + 1) - count_R_in(lo, hi)

    total -= sumD + sumE

    try:
        import numpy as np
    except Exception:
        np = None

    if np is not None:
        Ca = np.array(C, dtype=np.int64)
        Da = np.array(D, dtype=np.int64)
        Ea = np.array(E, dtype=np.int64)
        Ra = np.array(R, dtype=np.int64)

        # |C inter D'(i)| : pairs (c,d) with i = d - c
        diff = Da[:, None] - Ca[None, :]
        mask_cd = (diff >= 1) & (diff <= n) & (~np.isin(diff, Ra))
        Scd = int(mask_cd.sum())

        # |C inter D'(i) inter E'(i)| : same pairs, plus e = d - 2c in E
        ee = diff - Ca[None, :]
        Scde = int((mask_cd & np.isin(ee, Ea)).sum())
        del diff, ee, mask_cd

        # |C inter E'(i)| : pairs (c,e) with i = c + e
        s = Ca[:, None] + Ea[None, :]
        Sce = int(((s >= 1) & (s <= n) & (~np.isin(s, Ra))).sum())
        del s

        # |D'(i) inter E'(i)| : pairs (d,e) with d + e = 2i, column j = (d-e)/2
        sd = Da[:, None] + Ea[None, :]
        jd = Da[:, None] - Ea[None, :]
        even = (sd & 1) == 0
        i2 = sd >> 1
        j2 = jd >> 1
        Sde = int((even & (i2 >= 1) & (i2 <= n) & (j2 >= 1) & (j2 <= n)
                   & (~np.isin(i2, Ra))).sum())
        del sd, jd, even, i2, j2
    else:
        Scd = 0
        Scde = 0
        for d in D:
            d2 = d
            for c in C:
                i = d2 - c
                if 1 <= i <= n and i not in Rset:
                    Scd += 1
                    if (d2 - 2 * c) in Eset:
                        Scde += 1
        Sce = 0
        for c in C:
            for e in E:
                i = c + e
                if 1 <= i <= n and i not in Rset:
                    Sce += 1
        Sde = 0
        for d in D:
            for e in E:
                s2 = d + e
                if s2 & 1:
                    continue
                i = s2 >> 1
                if 1 <= i <= n and i not in Rset:
                    j = d - i
                    if 1 <= j <= n:
                        Sde += 1

    total += Scd + Sce + Sde - Scde
    sys.stdout.write(str(total) + "\n")

    linear = 0

        while i > 0:
